ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: “Rolling along, letting things run” recurs in verses and addresses for an unforced daily course, including eating at meal times and knowingly appearing simple.
EvidenceBody: Literally, rolling or buoyant and letting the course of things run : "rolling along, letting things run." The exact order occurs 79 times in 58 allowlisted texts; the reversed form "letting things run, rolling along" occurs 140 times in . In the Anquan lyric transmitted by the Collection of the Patriarchal Hall, eating gruel in the morning and another meal at midday leads directly to, "today, letting things run, rolling along; tomorrow, rolling along, letting things run," followed by "inside, clearly knowing it all, only feigning foolishness and binding up dullness" . Yuanwu places it after "thoroughly ordinary" . Gaofeng twice repeats both orders together; one passage describes a person who has no household property to return to and nothing named Chan to study, life-and-death to escape, or extinction to certify, and who spends the whole day "rolling along, letting things run; letting things run, rolling along." Feiyin uses the doubled reversible formula for walking, standing, sitting, lying, dressing, and eating, and elsewhere pairs it with "free and easy" and "cleanly fallen away" . Chan thus bends an ordinary adverbial expression into a rhythmic, reversible stock description attached to meals, ordinary activity, and appraisals of a person; the texts do not reduce it to a named procedure.
